content.user_title: Upgrade Dependencies With Release Note Verification
content.value_statement: Dependency upgrades can introduce breaking changes and obscure existing failures. This skill guides focused upgrades through release notes, baseline checks, targeted edits, and verification reports.
actual_capabilities: Identify installed versions from lockfiles and resolve explicit target versions with the package manager.
Review intermediate release notes and link breaking changes, runtime requirements, and deprecations to their sources.
Search the codebase for affected APIs and list impacted files before editing.
Update the selected dependency and required peers using the project package manager, then apply focused code changes.
Compare build, test, lint, and type-check results against a recorded baseline.
Report changes, verification results, warnings, and rollback guidance.
limitations: Requires an assistant with access to project files and tools; the skill itself is a written workflow.
Release-note completeness and available project checks limit how thoroughly compatibility can be assessed.
Runtime or peer version increases require user confirmation before changes proceed.
Does not provide an automated vulnerability scanner or guarantee that an upgrade eliminates all defects.

use_cases.title: Maintain an application dependency
use_cases.description: Upgrade one application package, trace changed APIs, and compare verification results with the baseline.

use_cases.title: Prepare a framework migration
use_cases.description: Review major-version migration notes, identify runtime requirements, and plan focused changes with an application smoke check.

use_cases.title: Document a security maintenance update
use_cases.description: Upgrade a dependency and cite security advisories only when confirmed by official advisories or release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the upgrade target
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the installed version of [package] from the lockfile and resolve the latest available version. Report both before making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish current and target versions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an upgrade of [package] from [current] to [target]. Review intermediate release notes, link breaking changes, and list affected files before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a focused upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade [package] to [target]. Record baseline checks, update through the package manager, apply required migrations, and compare verification results. Ask before runtime changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: implement and verify the change.

prompt_templates.title: Handle migration conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade [package] to [target] with required peers only. Show transitive conflicts and options without overrides. Request approval for runtime or peer version increases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: manage coupled dependencies and compatibility conflicts.

output_examples.input: Plan a major-version dependency upgrade before editing.
output: Version review: installed and target versions identified; release-note sources linked.
Impact review: removed APIs and affected project files listed.
Approval needed: the target release requires a newer runtime.

output_examples.input: Summarize a completed dependency upgrade and its verification.
output: Scope: the selected package, required peers, lockfile, and affected API usages were updated.
Verification: build and type checks passed; the same pre-existing test failure remains.
Follow-up: a deprecation warning remains documented.
Rollback: revert the upgrade commit and restore dependencies using the project package manager.

best_practices: Start with a clean working tree and record existing verification failures before upgrading.
Review every intervening release and cite source links for relevant breaking changes.
Keep changes focused and report skipped checks, remaining warnings, and rollback steps.
anti_patterns: Running a blanket dependency update or mixing the upgrade with unrelated refactoring.
Skipping failing tests or loosening version ranges to conceal incompatibilities.
Overriding transitive conflicts or increasing runtime requirements without review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The listed tools are Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Project edits and command execution require appropriate tool access.

faq.question: Can it upgrade every dependency at once?
faq.answer: No. The workflow targets one dependency or a tightly coupled group, including required peers.

faq.question: How does it determine the latest version?
faq.answer: It asks the package manager for available versions and states the exact target number before proceeding.

faq.question: What happens when release notes are unavailable?
faq.answer: It reports the missing release notes and treats the upgrade as higher risk.

faq.question: Does it automatically change runtime requirements?
faq.answer: No. It must stop and request confirmation before increasing minimum runtime or peer dependency versions.

faq.question: Does it verify security advisory claims?
faq.answer: It names an advisory only when supported by an official advisory or release notes. It does not provide independent vulnerability scanning.
